content_text: Add a paragraph, as reminded by a friend, I will say it here: In the Peng Yu case, it was finally confirmed that Peng Yu was indeed the one who knocked down the elderly man, but later there were too many incidents of 'bad people becoming old,' which led many people to subconsciously believe that Peng Yu was innocent. Will good people still be rewarded? This question now troubles countless Chinese people. Law enforcement authorities must put an end to the practice of compromise and guard the bottom line of the rule of law! A news story titled 'Tree too easy to climb, claim of 600,000 yuan' has sparked heated discussion among netizens. Clicking on the news is really surprising: a 60-year-old man surnamed Wu in Guangzhou was climbing a tree to pick bayberries while visiting a scenic spot, when a rotten branch broke, causing Wu to fall from the tree, and he died despite emergency treatment at the hospital. Afterwards, Wu’s family believed that the scenic spot had failed to take safety guidance or management measures to prevent risks, and claimed more than 600,000 yuan from the scenic spot. Even more bizarre was the court’s ruling: the Guangzhou Huadu District Court in the first instance ruled that Wu, as an adult, had climbed the tree without consent and should have anticipated the danger, and should bear the main responsibility for his own damage; the defendant scenic spot, for failing to warn of the danger, should bear 5% of the liability, and pay 45,000 yuan in compensation. Honestly, the result of the first-instance judgment left my heart extremely confused. First, you stole my things and fell to your death, and I did not ask you to return my fruit and tree, but you still successfully extorted money from me? Then next time if someone suffers heatstroke or dies while queuing in a scenic spot, is it to sue the scenic spot for not informing them to bring an umbrella, or to sue Hou Yi for not shooting down all the suns?! Secondly, how should a scenic spot inform of dangers? Should it assign a security guard to each visitor, or put up a warning sign at every possible accident location? A sign under the tree: 'Trees are fragile, please do not climb!' A sign on the small fence next to the tree: 'Fence has corners, be careful!' A sign on the path next to the fence: 'The path is not flat, beware of sprains!' Oh, and each lychee must also carry a warning label: 'Contains a pit, choking hazard!' If this were the case, would anyone still be willing to visit scenic spots? Moreover, even if the scenic spot had perfect safety measures and proper emergency response, could such a tragedy have been avoided? The answer is: it might help, but tragedies can never be completely prevented. Because no matter how dense the warnings, how thoughtful the security measures, or how professional the medical staff, they cannot save a person who does not follow the rules. And the court’s compromising judgment has unintentionally encouraged the social malpractice of 'the crying child gets the candy'! 01 I die, I am right Do you remember the 'elevator anti-smoking sudden death case'? Half a year ago, Mr. Yang from Henan Province advised an old man not to smoke in the elevator of a residential community, which caused an argument, and the old man became so emotional that he suffered a heart attack and died. Later, the old man’s family sued him in court, claiming 400,000 yuan. In the first trial, the court decided that Mr. Yang should pay 15,000 yuan in compensation, which caused a social uproar. Even more ridiculous was that the family was not satisfied and continued to appeal, and as a result, the second-instance verdict came out: the persuader was not responsible and did not need to pay any money. The second-instance verdict came out, and it was truly satisfying! Smoking is prohibited in the elevator, did you not see the big characters? Good people are maintaining social order, while those who break the rules are talking about 'dignity' with confidence. When he died suddenly because of his dignity, his family actually had the nerve to sue the good man in court, and shamelessly said: Why do you criticize him from the moral high ground? Haha, why? Just because you: 'I am old, I am right,' 'I am weak, I am right,' 'I am dead, I am right,' 'pseudo-moral bitches' are harming the entire moral system of society! 02 Murdering morality! Good people are not rewarded Law and morality are the two main tools for maintaining long-term public security in China. When the law has blind spots, morality becomes the only bond of trust between people. However, a group of people in China are waving the banner of 'morality' to profit and harm society! The Peng Yu case opened up an industry. Do you still remember the Peng Yu case? Of course, the focus of the Peng Yu case is not on the outcome of the trial, but on its subsequent impact. In the words of one netizen, the Peng Yu case is a milestone in the decline of morality in China, and it opened up the most distorted industry among the elderly in China: the 'touching porcelain' industry. The current situation under the 'touching porcelain' industry: fear of helping is like facing a tiger, and everyone feels unsafe! Last December, three middle school students in Shangrao, Jiangxi Province, saw an old lady fall on their way home from school, and they hurried to help her up. As a result, the old lady said to them that she wanted 100,000 yuan for hospitalization. Fortunately, two passing college students helped check the surveillance and resolved the dispute. However, although the good students were praised, the bad person was not harmed in the slightest except for criticism. A certain netizen did statistics. As of October 2017, among 149 cases that caused controversy due to helping others, about 80% of the cases were finally clarified. Among them, there were 32 cases of people pretending to be good people and hitting others, and 84 cases of falsely accusing those who helped. Among the 84 cases in which the people who were helped turned against their benefactors, only one case was punished with detention, but because the offender was over 70 years old, it was decided not to be executed according to law. This is the legacy of the Peng Yu case. Some bad people use people’s morality to deliberately touch porcelain and extort. If they succeed, they will have a lot of wealth; if they fail, at most they will only be criticized. Therefore, after the Peng Yu case, porcelain-touching security checks have sprung up like mushrooms after rain. Someone said that similar cases are telling: more than 40 years of Lei Feng education, and one Peng Yu case pushed us back before the liberation. 03 If not rectified, social morality will collapse In fact, whether it is the Peng Yu case or the elevator anti-smoking case, the focus is not that good people are not rewarded, but the toxic aftereffects these incidents have produced: the Chinese are being forced into indifference, and the 5,000-year-old moral system of China is plummeting. Last year, a girl in Zhumadian, Henan Province, was hit by a taxi on the road, and the driver fled. The girl lay on the cold road, and passersby ignored her. A mother hugged her frightened child and quickly left, and students on bicycles nearby looked and walked away. Finally, a speeding car ran over her again, taking her life! The video was uploaded online, and some lamented the coldness of the world, while others denounced the ruthlessness of China. Indeed, what they said was true, but few, knowing it, dared to face the underlying reason. With the phrase: 'If you did not hit me, why did you help?' When countless people were blackmailed to bankruptcy, when one hit-and-run case after another ended without result, it seemed that overnight, the entire educational orientation changed. All parents taught their children not to help others, especially the elderly and children; all teachers taught students not to do good deeds easily, because most likely you will be blackmailed; how many parents called their children at night, with tears begging their children not to show off; how many teachers lamented in class: 'I am supposed to teach and educate, but I have to go against my conscience and advise you to learn to protect yourself and not to do things that are not your own business.' It is no exaggeration to say that with one after another 'good people not rewarded but punished' incident, China’s public morality has regressed by more than 500 years. If it is not rectified, morality will be in danger, society will be in danger, and the nation will be in danger! 04 The year 2018, the first year of social moral reconstruction This year, 2018, is destined to be the most important year in the moral history of China. Taking advantage of the 'elevator anti-smoking sudden death case,' from the central to the local, a trend of reshaping social morality and encouraging the people to carry forward public spirit is forming a storm, sweeping across the country. On January 23, after the Zhengzhou Intermediate People’s Court rejected the Tian family’s second-instance appeal and denied Mr. Yang’s 15,000 yuan compensation in the first instance, the People’s Daily published an article titled 'Dissuasion should be encouraged by law' to set the record straight.
